clue.text: Crowd sustained energy in festive gathering

parts.note: to crowd is to jam, pack tightly
sustained, tediously drawn out, as a verb is bore: to weary someone
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A packed crowd keeps up its energy at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustained' reads as keeping something going, but here it is the verb bore, to weary by going on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively celebration or rally, a party on a big scale.

clue.text: Biblical characters' names in miscellaneous collection

parts.note: Job is the patient sufferer of the Old Testament
Lot is Abraham's nephew who fled Sodom

explanation.surface: A list of Bible figures' names in an assorted collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'names in' links the pieces to the definition. A job lot is a British term for a mixed batch sold as one lot at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is an assortment of goods sold together as a single unit.

clue.text: Stuff to count

explanation.surface: A two-part instruction to fill and tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is a noun here, not the verb to fill; 'count' is to be important.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter is substance or material; and to matter is to be significant, to carry weight.

clue.text: A scone, crackers and lots of water

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tea-time scone and some crackers, plus a good deal to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like more food alongside the scone, but it is the anagram signal working on A SCONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seas covering most of the globe are vast bodies of water.

clue.text: Heroic work, involving start of spire, consumed bishop's term of office

indicators.note: involving means the word for heroic takes in another letter

parts.note: epic means heroic, on a grand scale

indicators.note: start of asks for the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A great building project, beginning with the spire, absorbed a bishop's time in office.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the first letter of spire, goes inside EPIC after its I, making EPISC.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcopate is the office or tenure of a bishop.

clue.text: Split stick

explanation.surface: Two terse words that pull in opposite directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is its own opposite: to cleave wood is to split it, while to cleave to someone is to cling.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses with contrary meanings: chop apart, and adhere closely.

clue.text: Speech with passage containing good joke about university

indicators.note: containing means the word for passage holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage or alley

indicators.note: about means the joke wraps around the abbreviation for university

parts.note: a gag is a good joke, a comedian's line

explanation.surface: An address including a witty remark aimed at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the university letter into the joke, and 'containing' puts that inside the passage; 'with' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Language is a system of speech, the words people use to talk.

clue.text: Disloyal, tasteless material penned by one with attitude

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one

indicators.note: penned by means the cheap stuff is enclosed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pose is an attitude, a posture struck
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Someone striking a pose writes vulgar, disloyal stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT goes between the S and E of APOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, so the word works as an adjective for renegade or faithless.

clue.text: Seven and ace after a shuffle disappear

indicators.note: the cards are shuffled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A seven and an ace vanish from the deck once it has been shuffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; the fodder is SEVEN plus ACE, eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to fade away and vanish like vapour.

clue.text: Anticlimactic book man put in loft

indicators.note: put in tells us the word for man goes inside the word for loft

parts.note: a loft is an attic, the room under the roof
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A book about a man stashed in the loft turns out to be a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man put in loft' reads as someone stuck in an attic, but 'put in' is the container signal splitting the loft word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a sudden drop from the lofty to the trivial, so something bathetic is a let-down, an anticlimax.

clue.text: Cat's name in past associated with Egyptian god

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name within the word for past

parts.note: ago means in the past, gone by
Ra is the ancient Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A cat named after an ancient Egyptian deity, as cats often were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat's' is the definition plus 's meaning 'has', a link; 'associated with' also only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a long-haired breed of domestic cat named after Ankara in Turkey.

clue.text: Excessively fussy rule, not good, that's broken by Conservative

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is to be dropped from the word for rule

parts.note: to rule is to govern

indicators.note: broken by means the abbreviation for that is split open with another letter put in

parts.note: that's, meaning that is, is i.e. (id est)

explanation.surface: A pedantic regulation is being flouted by a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: GOVERN without G gives OVERN; IE split by C gives ICE. 'that's' stands for 'that is', the Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-nice means too fastidious or particular, nice in its old sense of precise and finicky.

clue.text: Servant with no right to receive shilling for activity

indicators.note: to receive means the trimmed word for servant takes in another letter
with no right says the letter for right is removed from the word for servant

parts.note: a butler is a senior household servant
S was the abbreviation for the shilling, an old British coin worth 12 pence

explanation.surface: A footman docked his rights is paid a shilling for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTLER less R is BUTLE, which takes S after BU. The shilling, abbreviated s, was a British coin used before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle is busy, energetic movement, a flurry of activity.

clue.text: Completely renovated great hotel

indicators.note: renovated means done up and remade, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A grand hotel given a total makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' looks like it modifies 'renovated', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means wholly, entirely.

clue.text: Rueful record kept by Auden's beginning like much of his work

indicators.note: beginning asks for the first letter of the poet's name
kept by means the word for record sits held within the descriptive word

parts.note: W. H. Auden was a poet, so much of his work is poetic
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A remorseful note preserved among Auden's early writings, as lyrical as his verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' tempts as a gramophone disc; here it is a logbook, and 'kept by' places it inside the adjective describing Auden's output.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry and contrite for a fault is rueful, full of regret.

clue.text: Resort's endless attraction captured by one account after another, with love

indicators.note: captured by means the trimmed word for attraction is held inside the accounts
one account after another asks for the abbreviation for account written twice
after another completes the instruction to repeat the account abbreviation
endless says the final letter of the word for attraction is cut off

parts.note: pull is attraction, drawing power
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A holiday spot's charm wears off after one bill follows another.
explanation.walkthrough: PULL loses its end to give PUL, which sits inside ACAC after ACA; O follows. ''s' stands for 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a Pacific beach resort on Mexico's coast.

clue.text: Mezzanine floor resident resolutely conserves

indicators.note: conserves means the phrase keeps the letters preserved within it

explanation.surface: Someone living on a mezzanine stubbornly saves things.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from residENT to RESOLutely.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a low storey between ground and first floor, a mezzanine.

clue.text: Spiteful volume, massive, written with no end of rancour

indicators.note: no here means the given letter is taken away from the word for massive

parts.note: massive means enormous

indicators.note: end of picks the first end letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A big, spiteful book written without a trace of bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of rancour' removes R, rancour's first letter, from the word for massive, leaving ENOMOUS; 'written with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous means full of malice, poisonous in attitude.

clue.text: Pleased one working to formulate argument

parts.note: pleased means content, satisfied
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means working, operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A satisfied person gets busy building a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to formulate' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A contention is a point asserted in a debate, a claim one argues for.

clue.text: Research scientist's away filling receptacle

indicators.note: filling means the word for away goes inside the container word

parts.note: a bin is a receptacle
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A scientist is off on business, leaving a container to be filled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scientist's' is 'scientist is'. Boffin is British slang for a research scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a technical expert, especially a lab researcher.

clue.text: Whip up cabbage? Not a challenge

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for whip is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: Not a says the letter A is removed from the word for cabbage

parts.note: kale is a variety of cabbage

explanation.surface: A cook is told to whisk cabbage, but it is not much of a task.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT read upwards gives TAC; KALE less A gives KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle is to take on or confront, as in a challenge.

clue.text: You'll be entertained by celebrity, one renowned for stamina

indicators.note: entertained by means the old word for you is welcomed inside the word for celebrity

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
ye is the old form of you; the 'll joins the clue together

explanation.surface: A fan will be treated by a famous name known for endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' is the container signal. A stayer is a horse or runner good over long distances.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a competitor with staying power, able to last the distance.

clue.text: A child, a human being

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds per (a) head
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A child is simply a human being.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'A' is read as 'per' (so much a day = so much per day).
explanation.definitionFit: A person is an individual, any man, woman or child.

clue.text: Booming hooter's returned — speak vehemently about it

indicators.note: about means the word for speak vehemently goes around the other piece

parts.note: to rant is to speak loudly and wildly

indicators.note: returned says the word for hooter is read backwards

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A loud horn has come back, and someone rails against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the nose round to ESON, and 'about' wraps the ranting word around it; 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant voice is deep and reverberating, loud and full.

clue.text: Rebuke? It's what stripper should have as performance proceeds

definitions.text: It's what stripper should have as performance proceeds

explanation.surface: A strip show prompting a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as LESS ON: a stripper wears less and less clothing as the act goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a reprimand meant to teach someone; and a striptease leaves the performer with fewer garments on.

clue.text: What offers access to any capital one may need if pressed?

definitions.text: What offers access to any capital one may need if pressed?

parts.words: What offers access to any capital one may need if pressed
parts.note: reads like a cash machine or emergency funds, but capital here is a capital letter, reached by holding down a button on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A source of ready money for anyone short of funds in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money and 'pressed' suggests hard up; in fact it is an upper-case letter and a key being pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a keyboard this key, when held down, types letters in upper case.

clue.text: Solemn-looking buff cutting out page about Western

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word for buff wraps around the abbreviation for Western
cutting out page says the letter for page is removed from the word for buff

parts.note: to buff is to polish, rub to a shine
W is the abbreviation for Western or west

explanation.surface: Someone polishing a cowboy film script with a stern face.
explanation.walkthrough: POLISH less P is OLISH, which goes around W after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking like an owl, with a grave, wise, bespectacled air, is a solemn appearance.

clue.text: Splendour for all to see maintained by two monarchs

indicators.note: maintained by means the letter for universal viewing is held inside the monarchs' letters

parts.note: two monarchs is read as GR and ER, the royal ciphers of George and Elizabeth, joined by the word and
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A grand spectacle open to everyone, supported by a royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The two monarchs spell out as GR and ER, the joining 'and' included; U sits inside before the final R. U was the British film rating for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is magnificence, impressive splendour and dignity.
